hints.title: Monthly Department vs Company Mean Benchmark
hints.text: Compare average department compensation against overall company average compensation for each pay month.

hints.title: Dual Window and Department Mean Comparison
hints.text: Format pay_date to year-month strings. Compute monthly department average and overall monthly company average, then label department as higher, lower, or same.

hints.title: Comparison Blueprint
hints.text: With Dept as (select date_format(pay_date, "%Y-%m") as pay_month, department_id, avg(amount) as dept_avg from Salary s join Employee e on s.employee_id = e.employee_id group by pay_month, department_id), Comp as (select date_format(pay_date, "%Y-%m") as pay_month, avg(amount) as comp_avg from Salary group by pay_month) select d.pay_month, d.department_id, case when d.dept_avg > c.comp_avg then "higher" when d.dept_avg < c.comp_avg then "lower" else "same" end as comparison from Dept d join Comp c on d.pay_month = c.pay_month order by d.pay_month desc, d.department_id asc.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH DeptAvg AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_FORMAT(s.pay_date, '%Y-%m') AS pay_month,
        e.department_id,
        AVG(s.amount) AS dept_avg
    FROM Salary s
    JOIN Employee e ON s.employee_id = e.employee_id
    GROUP BY pay_month, e.department_id
),
CompAvg AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_FORMAT(pay_date, '%Y-%m') AS pay_month,
        AVG(amount) AS comp_avg
    FROM Salary
    GROUP BY pay_month
)
SELECT 
    d.pay_month,
    d.department_id,
    CASE 
        WHEN d.dept_avg > c.comp_avg THEN 'higher'
        WHEN d.dept_avg < c.comp_avg THEN 'lower'
        ELSE 'same'
    END AS comparison
FROM DeptAvg d
JOIN CompAvg c ON d.pay_month = c.pay_month
ORDER BY d.pay_month DESC, d.department_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Grouped monthly averages and join execution scale in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Row-by-row correlated subqueries compute whole-table averages repeatedly for each department.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pre-aggregating monthly company averages avoids redundant scans.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of DATE_FORMAT for monthly normalization and CASE expression comparisons.

import pandas as pd

def average_salary_departments_vs_company(salary: pd.DataFrame, employee: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = salary.merge(employee, on='employee_id')
    df['pay_month'] = pd.to_datetime(df['pay_date']).dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
    
    comp_avg = df.groupby('pay_month')['amount'].mean().to_dict()
    dept_avg = df.groupby(['pay_month', 'department_id'])['amount'].mean().reset_index()
    
    dept_avg['comp_avg'] = dept_avg['pay_month'].map(comp_avg)
    dept_avg['comparison'] = 'same'
    dept_avg.loc[dept_avg['amount'] > dept_avg['comp_avg'], 'comparison'] = 'higher'
    dept_avg.loc[dept_avg['amount'] < dept_avg['comp_avg'], 'comparison'] = 'lower'
    
    res = dept_avg[['pay_month', 'department_id', 'comparison']]
    return res.sort_values(by=['pay_month', 'department_id'], ascending=[False, True])
